narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Slightly cooler and cloudier than yesterday; winds little changed. Dry by day, with thunder possible, peaking overnight again. 30°C (87°F) high, 20°C (67°F) low. Sky mostly clear early as reported, mostly clear at midday and partly cloudy in the evening. Wind NE early and SW at midday; gusts to 38 km/h (20 kt). UV index 8.9 (very high). Air quality 124 (unhealthy for sensitive groups) at Kisumu Airport, the highest of 3 stations. As of 07:04, reports through 06:30: no rain; no thunder; high so far 19°C (66°F); low so far 19°C (66°F); peak sustained 4 km/h (2 kt); sky mostly clear.

## Extended Outlook

Temperatures and winds much the same through Saturday, with thunderstorms likely each day. Skies partly cloudy throughout. Saturday's call: dry, 30%, with one of four models wet; highs around 32°C (89°F). At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 93% of the time over 98 checks.

Further out, temperatures and winds much the same through Wednesday, with thunderstorms possible Sunday, thunderstorms likely Monday, showers and thunderstorms possible Tuesday, and dry Wednesday with thunderstorms possible. Sunday: no model wet, highs 31 to 33°C (88 to 92°F), thunder possible rather than likely. Monday: no model wet, highs 31 to 33°C (87 to 92°F), thunder likely rather than possible. Tuesday: one of three models wet, the week's wettest day at 2 mm (0.07 in) on average, highs around 32°C (90°F), thunder possible rather than likely.

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Monday. Wednesday's call: rain, 59%, with one of two models wet; highs 29 to 33°C (85 to 92°F). At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 93% of the time over 94 checks.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Convective instability in the hours ahead: UKMO 2580 J/kg, ICON 1940 J/kg, ECMWF 1890 J/kg and GFS 610 J/kg. Thunder likely; any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above the 38 km/h (20 kt) forecast.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Peak gust 31 km/h (17 kt). Any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above this figure; the water is unsafe while one is nearby.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1010 hPa) and highest toward the northeast (1016 hPa) — a 6 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the north is deepening over the next three days. Pressure is also falling toward the northwest — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is falling. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across the basin's 5 points, pressure today sits between 1013.5 and 1015.8 hPa, falling by 2.0 hPa over three days. Pressure here over the last 24 hours: -0.6 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

On rain the record ranks ECMWF first at Day+3, right 93% of the last 30 checks and ECMWF first at Day+7, right 93% of the last 30 checks. On today's high ICON is the warmest model at 30.0°C (86.0°F) and ECMWF the coolest at 28.5°C (83.3°F); the call's 30.3°C (86.5°F) sits at the warm end. At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others here yet. At Day+3, ECMWF is the strongest rain caller here and kenya_met the weakest. At Day+7, ECMWF is the strongest rain caller here and GFS the weakest.

Figures issued 07:04. Written by code; a discussion follows when a model answers.
